title: OA MARTIAL ARTS OPENER - the doctrine prose through the Styles intro: the three reason strands, the regularized art, the proliferation and the five style characteristics
audit_label: R688 OA martial arts opener audit
audit_comment: OA round seventy-five (capture pp. 223-224): the Martial Arts opener - the doctrine frame with the three reason strands, the regularized art, the style proliferation and the five style characteristics, single-pass pins per the Chapter 9 provenance shift

banner.title: OA MARTIAL ARTS OPENER, printed capture pp. 223-224 - the doctrine prose round
banner.provenance: pinned from the 2018 print capture - the sole surviving pass per the R679 provenance shift. THE FRAME: the martial arts a combat style unique to these lands - the body into a weapon, hands, feet, legs, arms, head, defeating the better armed and armored through rigorous training and deep discipline. THE THREE REASONS: the nature-forces philosophy (living in harmony, the tools intruding upon it), the religious divestment (only the inner qualities permanent), the social pressure (the weapon-restriction edicts, torture and execution, the commoners unarmed). THE ART: regularized, studied, guiding the student to self-perfection. THE PROLIFERATION: every land its own styles against the local weapons and the beasts, each master his own moves - the school challenges the spectator events. THE GOAL: the fighter trained to avoid being hurt - the defensive, aggressive and weapon-master schools; the near-infinite forms; the unarmed misnomer with the tui-fu; the styles defined by their effects, the five characteristics grouping into a style. The prose codifies per the R431 calculus

consts.name: djbOAMartialStyleChars
consts.comment: the five style characteristics - the martial arts classified by number of attacks, damage, armor class, principal attack form and special maneuvers, the elements grouped together forming a style (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialArtsDoctrine
bools.comment: the doctrine frame - the martial arts a style of combat that never developed significantly in the rest of the AD&D world, the body developed into a useful weapon defeating opponents supposedly better armed and armored (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialWholeBodyWeapon
bools.comment: the whole-body rule - the unarmed fighter uses his entire body - hands, feet, legs, arms, head - any part turned into a weapon, through rigorous training demanding great physical and mental discipline (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialTrainingDiscipline
bools.comment: the training clause - the unarmed fighter must learn to anticipate actions, harden his body, block out pain, and summon energies from deep within himself, a deep commitment on the part of the character (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialNaturePhilosophy
bools.comment: the nature philosophy - the belief in the forces of nature surrounding and charging everything with hidden energies, the character part of them drawing upon them, living in harmony; tools effective but outside the harmony, intruding upon it - understanding one's own body one factor leading to unarmed skill (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialReligiousDivestment
bools.comment: the religious strand - material possessions of little real worth, the devout divesting themselves of the desire for the material world, only the inner qualities permanent and positively known; reliance upon a weapon reliance upon the material world (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialSocialPressure
bools.comment: the social strand - severe edicts restricting weapon ownership in conquered lands and troublesome provinces, punishments including torture and execution, the commoners finding other ways to defend themselves (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialRegularizedArt
bools.comment: the regularization - the skills widely practiced and honorable, the styles and training practices regularized, careful study of scientific principles and religious concepts, unarmed fighting an art guiding the student to self-perfection when practiced diligently and correctly (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialStyleProliferation
bools.comment: the proliferation - every land its own styles countering the locally favored weapons and studying the natural styles of the beasts, each master his own moves and methods - two masters of the same style easily fighting in entirely different forms (print capture p. 223)

bools.name: djbOAMartialSchoolChallenges
bools.comment: the school challenges - arguments and challenges over which style was better quite common, the fighters of different schools seeking supremacy, often spectator events with hundreds of interested onlookers (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialPrimaryGoalAvoidHurt
bools.comment: the primary goal - at the lowest level the martial arts train the fighter in the use of his body, the primary goal that he can avoid being hurt (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialDefensiveStyles
bools.comment: the defensive schools - some styles mainly defensive, diverting or avoiding the attack (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialAggressiveStyles
bools.comment: the aggressive schools - other styles more aggressive, their masters believing that attacking is the best way to protect oneself (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialWeaponMasterStyles
bools.comment: the weapon-master schools - others demanding the fighter learn and master many different weapons to understand their use (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialFormsVariety
bools.comment: the forms variety - punches, blocks, kicks, pushes, throws, holds, locks and dodges, a near infinite variety of moves depending mainly on the style learned (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialUnarmedMisnomer
bools.comment: the misnomer - unarmed combat also a misnomer: students often expected to learn common and unusual weapons, their use taught only as part of a particular martial arts style - the tui-fu foolish in peasant hands but deadly in the hands of a master of martial arts (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialRulesFit
bools.comment: the rules fit - the martial arts designed to fit within the AD&D rules, the styles defined by their effects - number of attacks, damage, armor class and principal attack form, the special maneuvers coming only with dedication and training (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialStyleNames
bools.comment: the style names - styles given descriptive or poetic names: animal names (Snake, Monkey, Tiger), poetic names (Eight Drunken Fairies), descriptive names (Empty Hand, Springing Legs, Eight Fists), each identifying a particular style (print capture p. 224)

bools.name: djbOAMartialStyleUseIdentity
bools.comment: the style use identity - styles further identified by their use, some highly defensive relying on the inner power of the user, others aggressive stressing form and channeled power in hard and sudden attacks (print capture p. 224)
